children: Micron Technology Inc. (MU, Financials), a major manufacturer of memory chips used in standard artificial intelligence (AI) systems and other gadgets, is confronting a new labor risk at one of its most critical manufacturing sites.
A union for workers at Micron's Taoyuan facility in Taiwan said it may call for a strike vote if talks on September 18 and 21 do not make sufficient progress. Timing is unfortunate for Micron.
The demand for high bandwidth memory used in AI infrastructure is still strong and Taiwan plays an important role in the company's DRAM and HBM production.
The union is asking Micron to implement a permanent scheme to share 15 percent of operating profit with workers globally.

Micron has already paid bonuses to more than 60,000 workers following what company dubbed a extraordinary year. Employees in Taiwan employed before Aug. 29, 2025 who are eligible will get a cash incentive of T$1 million, or about $31,500.

Workers think it is not enough. They want a permanent profit sharing scheme not a one time payout. The dispute is of significant scope. Two of the unions in mediation represent more than 80% of Micron's 15,000 or so employees in Taiwan.
Investors definitely have Sept. 18 and 21 on the calendar. If negotiations go through, the labor conflict might become a production risk at just the worst period in the AI memory cycle.

title: Micron's AI boom just ran into an unexpected labor problem
